searchText: That’s fair. I’m just suggesting perhaps that the bottleneck isn’t really the sequencer, which I view as more of a redundancy and network resiliency issue. Maybe there’s a happy medium where you get benefits of resiliency & uptime with distributing the sequencer set more than they are today (early days obviously) but maintaining the large design space to innovate on execution & performance (some of the StarkNet rendering stuff from guiltygyoza is kind of remarkable). Rather it’s having a working proof system + lots of people verifying what the rollups post to L1, and continuing to push on that via trust-minimized light clients I guess it’s all a matter of finding the optimal trade-offs points to maximize against 🤷‍♂️ Too many people trade off censorship resistance IMO (see all L2s available today). I think we need at least *some* L2s, particularly zkRollups, to be censorship resistant. If all we have is censorship resistant L1 and a bunch of censorable L2s I feel like we haven't achieved scaling of Ethereum. While I agree, I doubt we will see much progress until the L2s are more complete and have much lower fees. If token swaps are under a penny, then focus will hopefully shift more towards censorship. This won't happen if the designs rely on censorability to achieve high throughput.
